prompt:
Style: color-block-breakout. Transform the supplied ORIGINAL photograph of a LEGO Millennium Falcon model on a white cabinet, minifigures, a display plaque and nearby autumn foliage. Render only a single full-frame artwork using this style treatment:

- **artwork — selection.** Analyze only the current photo (never combine photos or reuse subjects, colors or design elements from earlier images). Pick its strongest subject, silhouette, gesture and relationship; compress 2–5 memorable cues into one dominant motif plus at most one supporting element. Remove roughly 85–90% of secondary background, objects, texture and clutter. - **artwork — style.** Bold simplified silhouettes, a few flat shapes, selective contours, and paper-white negative space — recognizable at phone size. About 65–75% of the lower panel stays clean warm-white paper, with generous margins and a visible paper gap at the midpoint. - **Palette.** At most two ink colors, both drawn only from the current photo's subject or defining cues, plus warm-white paper. The lighter, quieter ink is used for the painted field; the darker, stronger ink for the focal subject. Colors stay mostly flat and matte — no black outlines, no accent colors, no complex gradients, no realistic shading, no noticeable third color. - **The breakout.** One compact, roughly rectangular painted field (about 20–25% of the lower panel, with soft irregular handmade edges — not a frame or cutout) holds most of the motif. Exactly one meaningful, source-derived part — flowing hair, an extended hand, a wing, a leg, a branch, an instrument, an architectural contour — extends clearly beyond one selected edge as one continuous, readable silhouette. That single extension is the poster's main surprise. - **Avoid list.** Side-by-side layouts, extra panels, tracing the whole photo, a monochrome filter, invented gestures, distorted anatomy, multiple competing extensions, floating decorative fragments, and any lower-panel element touching or crossing into the upper photo. 

Preserve the original scene's subject relationships. Every part of the canvas must belong to the transformed artwork. No original photo panel, no before/after comparison, no split, no text.
reference_method: isolated single-source batch; image results withheld until all calls completed; per-image Git checkpoint
